_about: Everyday events (Stage 6.1). Format in docs/STAGE_6_EVENTS.md. Text fields fill {player}, {first}, {club}, {short}, {city}, {stadium}, {coach}, {assistant}, {person}, {amount}, {half}, {double}, {sponsor} and {opponent}. Effects: cash (x amount, with line), fans, mood (the player), squad, press, goodwill, flag, price (ticket price share), promise, later.

events.title: {player} wants to play
events.text: {player} knocks on the door. "I came here to play football, not to keep the bench warm. Give me a chance, or tell me straight if I'm not in your plans."

choices.label: Promise him three starts
choices.hint: He will expect 3 starts in the next 6 weeks. Keep your word or he'll take it badly.
choices.result: {first} leaves smiling. The coach has been told.

choices.label: Tell him to fight for his place
choices.hint: No promises. He won't love it.
choices.result: {first} nods, jaw set. Training should be lively this week.

choices.label: Say he's part of the plan
choices.hint: A small lift, but words wear thin without minutes.
choices.result: {first} seems reassured, for now.

events.title: {player}'s agent calls
events.text: {player}'s agent wants to know where things stand. "My client has a year left. He loves {city}, but other clubs are asking. Are we talking about a new deal or not?"

choices.label: Say you want him for years
choices.hint: He'll be pleased. Renew his contract on the Squad screen while he's happy.
choices.result: The agent sounds warm. "We'll be waiting for your offer."

choices.label: Talk in the off-season
choices.hint: Keeps your options open. He may feel undervalued.
choices.result: "Fine. But don't leave it too long."

choices.label: Tell him nobody is bigger than the club
choices.hint: Good for your image with the press, bad for the player.
choices.result: The line goes quiet. The press love the quote.

events.title: {sponsor} wants the players
events.text: {sponsor} are opening a new flagship store in {city} and want the squad there on Tuesday, signing shirts for two hours. They'll pay {amount} on top of the shirt deal.

choices.label: Send the whole squad
choices.hint: Earns {amount}. The players would rather rest.
choices.result: Queues round the block. The players smile through it.

choices.label: Send two senior players
choices.hint: Earns {half}. Everyone's happy enough.
choices.result: Two players, a lot of selfies, a decent cheque.

choices.label: Say no, the players need rest
choices.hint: No money, and the sponsor will remember.
choices.result: The sponsor's rep forces a smile. "Of course. Another time."

events.title: The children's ward asks for a visit
events.text: {person} from the club's community office says the children's ward at {city} General has asked if some players could visit before the holidays. They're also raising money for a new play room.

choices.label: Send players with presents
choices.hint: Costs {half}. Fans and the press will notice.
choices.result: A ward full of grins. One young fan made {coach} sign his cast.

choices.label: Fund the whole play room
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. A plaque with the club's name goes on the door.
choices.result: The play room will carry the club crest. The local paper runs it on page three.

choices.label: Not this year
choices.hint: Saves money. Looks cold.
choices.result: {person} looks disappointed but says they understand.

events.title: Fans' group: tickets cost too much
events.text: {person}, chair of the {short} Supporters' Trust, brings a petition. "Two thousand signatures. Families can't afford to come any more. Bring the prices down."

choices.label: Cut prices by 10%
choices.hint: Less money per ticket, more goodwill in the stands.
choices.result: Applause at the next Trust meeting. Prices drop 10%.

choices.label: Promise a review in the summer
choices.hint: Buys a little time.
choices.result: {person} takes the promise, but says they'll be watching.

choices.label: Explain the club needs the money
choices.hint: Honest, but the fans won't like it.
choices.result: {person} leaves unconvinced. There's talk of banners.

events.title: {coach} asks for a signing
events.text: {coach} closes the door. "We're one player short of something good. Get me someone who can make a difference this window and I'll do the rest."

choices.label: Promise a signing
choices.hint: Sign any player in the next 4 weeks, or {coach} will feel let down.
choices.result: {coach} shakes your hand. "That's all I needed to hear."

choices.label: Say you'll see what the money allows
choices.hint: No promises either way.
choices.result: "Fair enough. Don't take too long."

choices.label: Tell him to work with what he has
choices.hint: Saves money. The dressing room hears about it.
choices.result: {coach} says nothing for a moment. "Understood."

events.title: An interview request
events.text: {person} from the {city} Courier wants a long sit-down interview for the weekend edition. "Your story, in your words. Where's the club going?"

choices.label: Give them an hour
choices.hint: The press will like you more.
choices.result: A two-page spread with a flattering photo. Mostly flattering.

choices.label: Fifteen minutes, by phone
choices.hint: A small lift.
choices.result: A short piece. Polite, accurate, forgettable.

choices.label: Decline
choices.hint: The paper won't forget it.
choices.result: The weekend edition runs "Owner too busy for {city}?"

events.title: A fight in training
events.text: {coach} reports a scuffle between {player} and a team-mate after a hard tackle. "It's sorted, mostly. But the lads are watching what we do."

choices.label: Fine them both a week's wages
choices.hint: Brings in {amount}. Sends a message, and stings.
choices.result: Both fined. Training is very quiet the next day.

choices.label: Take the squad out for dinner
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. Clear the air.
choices.result: By dessert the two of them are laughing about it.

choices.label: Leave it with the coach
choices.hint: Nothing changes much.
choices.result: {coach} handles it: extra running for everyone.

events.title: The council and match-day parking
events.text: Councillor {person} has had complaints. "Cars on every pavement around {stadium} on match days. The residents want something done, and so do I."

choices.label: Pay for match-day shuttle buses
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. The council will remember the favour.
choices.result: Shuttle buses from the town centre. The councillor sends a thank-you note.

choices.label: Promise to look into it
choices.hint: Free, for now.
choices.result: "I'll hold you to that."

choices.label: Say parking is the council's problem
choices.hint: Free. The council may make life harder later.
choices.result: Councillor {person} leaves with a tight smile.

events.title: A guest for the directors' box
events.text: {person}, who owns half the waterfront in {city}, would like the best seats for the {opponent} match, and a table for eight. "Money's no object. Atmosphere is."

choices.label: Roll out the red carpet
choices.hint: Earns {amount} in hospitality.
choices.result: {person} leaves with a signed ball and a smile. The cheque clears.

choices.label: Offer pitch-side seats with the fans
choices.hint: Earns {half}. The fans like an owner who mixes.
choices.result: {person} loves it. Sings along by the second half.

choices.label: The box is full
choices.hint: No money.
choices.result: "Another time, perhaps."

events.title: {player} is unhappy
events.text: {player} looks tired of it all. "I don't feel wanted here. I'm not asking to leave, not yet, but something has to change."

choices.label: Promise him more football
choices.hint: He'll expect 3 starts in 6 weeks.
choices.result: {first} brightens a little. "Thank you. I won't let you down."

choices.label: Give him a loyalty bonus
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. Money talks, for a while.
choices.result: The bonus lands. {first} is smiling in training.

choices.label: Ask him to be patient
choices.hint: Free. Might not be enough.
choices.result: {first} shrugs. "We'll see."

events.title: The players want a bonus
events.text: {player} speaks for the dressing room. "Three wins on the bounce. The lads would like to see that rewarded, boss."

choices.label: Pay a win bonus
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. The squad will run through walls.
choices.result: Cheers from the dressing room. Someone puts music on.

choices.label: Team dinner on the club
choices.hint: Costs {half}. A nice gesture.
choices.result: Steak for everyone. The fitness coach winces.

choices.label: Winning is the bonus
choices.hint: Free. They'll grumble.
choices.result: "Right you are, boss." Nobody's smiling.

events.title: The fans want answers
events.text: Three defeats in a row. {person} from the Supporters' Trust is in reception. "People are angry. They want to hear it from you."

choices.label: Meet the fans in the club bar
choices.hint: Brave. Could go either way, but usually helps.
choices.result: Two hours of hard questions. They leave grudgingly respectful.

choices.label: Write an open letter
choices.hint: A small lift.
choices.result: The letter goes up on the club site. Some read it.

choices.label: Let results do the talking
choices.hint: Free, but the silence will be noticed.
choices.result: No comment. The radio phone-in has a field day.

events.title: A retro kit idea
events.text: {person} from the club shop has an idea: a limited run of the kit from the club's first ever season. "The old-timers will love it, and the kids think it's cool now."

choices.label: Order a big run
choices.hint: Costs {amount} now. Could sell well later.
choices.result: Boxes of retro shirts arrive at the shop.

effects.title: The retro kit sold out
effects.text: The retro shirts are gone. The shop made {double}.

choices.label: A small test run
choices.hint: Costs {half}. A safer bet.
choices.result: A few hundred shirts go on sale.

effects.title: Retro kit sales
effects.text: The small run sold steadily. The shop made {amount}.

choices.label: Not now
choices.hint: No cost.
choices.result: {person} puts the sketches back in the drawer.

events.title: The mascot wants a pay rise
events.text: The person inside the club mascot has written to you, formally, on headed paper. They want a raise, a new costume fan, and "respect". There are threats of a strike before the next home match.

choices.label: Pay up
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. Peace in our time.
choices.result: The mascot does a celebratory cartwheel. Mostly successfully.

choices.label: Wear the suit yourself next match
choices.hint: Free. The press will love it, or laugh at you.
choices.result: You do a full lap of the pitch in the suit. The video goes round the whole of {city}.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.hint: Free. The kids will miss the mascot.
choices.result: The mascot strikes. A cardboard cut-out stands in. It is not the same.

events.title: {player} out late before a match
events.text: {person} from the {city} Courier has photos of {player} leaving a club at 3am, two nights before the last match. "Care to comment before we print?"

choices.label: Fine him publicly
choices.hint: Brings in {amount}. Discipline looks good; he'll sulk.
choices.result: Fined and named. The paper calls it "strong leadership".

choices.label: Defend him: it was his day off
choices.hint: He'll love you for it. The paper won't.
choices.result: "He's young, it was his day off." {first} won't forget it.

choices.label: A quiet word, no comment
choices.hint: Small hits all round.
choices.result: The photos run anyway. {first} looks sheepish all week.

events.title: A documentary crew wants in
events.text: {person}, a producer, wants to film a behind-the-scenes series on {short} for the whole season. "Cameras in the dressing room, the boardroom, your office. Real stories."

choices.label: Full access
choices.hint: Earns {amount}. The players won't love the cameras.
choices.result: The crew moves in on Monday. Someone already tripped over a cable.

choices.label: Matches and training only
choices.hint: Earns {half}.
choices.result: A tidier show, fewer secrets.

choices.label: Decline
choices.hint: The dressing room stays private.
choices.result: "Your loss." They go and film someone else.

events.title: The storm wrecked the pitch
events.text: {person}, the head groundskeeper, is close to tears. Last night's storm flooded half the pitch at {stadium}. "I can patch it, or we can do it properly."

choices.label: Re-lay the damaged half
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. A perfect surface.
choices.result: New turf goes down overnight. {person} sleeps for the first time in days.

choices.label: Patch it up
choices.hint: Costs {half}. A bit bumpy.
choices.result: The pitch is playable. The players complain about the bounce.

choices.label: It'll dry out
choices.hint: Free. The players won't be happy.
choices.result: It does not dry out quickly. Training moves to the car park.

events.title: The oldest season-ticket holder
events.text: {person} turns 100 this month and has had a season ticket at {stadium} for 71 years. Their grandchildren ask if the club could do something special.

choices.label: Invite them to lead the team out
choices.hint: Free. A moment everyone will remember.
choices.result: {person} walks out to a standing ovation. Not a dry eye in the ground.

choices.label: Send a signed shirt
choices.hint: Free. A kind gesture.
choices.result: The shirt is framed above {person}'s favourite chair.

choices.label: Send a card
choices.hint: The bare minimum.
choices.result: A nice card. The grandchildren had hoped for more.

events.title: {player} has a boot offer
events.text: {player} is buzzing. A sports brand wants him as the face of their new boot, but they want him to film adverts on two training days.

choices.label: Let him do it, on his day off
choices.hint: He'll be thrilled. The club gets {amount} for image rights.
choices.result: {first} films the advert on his day off. The posters go up in {city}.

choices.label: Allow it on training days
choices.hint: Earns {double}. {coach} won't like it.
choices.result: Two training days lost. The advert is very shiny.

choices.label: Tell him to focus on football
choices.hint: He'll be gutted.
choices.result: {first} goes quiet. The brand signs someone else.

events.title: A testimonial for a club legend
events.text: {person}, who played 400 games for the club, is retiring from coaching. Their family asks if {stadium} could host a testimonial match, with the proceeds going to the club's youth foundation.

choices.label: Host it and cover the costs
choices.hint: Costs {amount}. The fans will love it.
choices.result: Twenty thousand turn up. Old heroes, slow legs, big cheers.

choices.label: Host it, split the gate
choices.hint: Costs nothing, earns nothing.
choices.result: A good day out. Everyone breaks even.

choices.label: The pitch needs rest
choices.hint: Free. Old fans will grumble.
choices.result: The match moves to the local park. The club gets no credit.
